title: Find a file by name using locate
summary: Use the `locate` command to quickly find files on your Mac by searching a pre-built database of filenames. This is faster than searching the entire disk manually, but it may not show files created very recently.

steps.explain: Search the locate database for files matching a specific pattern or name.

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: The filename or part of the filename you are looking for.

alternatives.explain: Search for a file by its exact filename (ignoring the path).

placeholders.name: FILENAME
placeholders.description: The exact name of the file.

alternatives.explain: Search for a pattern while ignoring case (uppercase/lowercase).
